actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Seed of the environment's random generator
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset

actions.description: Set the seed used by the simulated world's random number generators for subsequent steps, without resetting the world. The accepted seed is echoed in the receipt.

facts.text: The package registers four legacy OpenAI Gym environments through gym.envs.registration.register (Pendulum-Gazebo-v0, CartPoleDiscreteBalancing-Gazebo-v0, CartPoleContinuousBalancing-Gazebo-v0 and CartPoleContinuousSwingup-Gazebo-v0) with the GazeboRuntime entry point and max_episode_steps=5000
CartPoleDiscreteBalancing-Gazebo-v0 is registered with task_cls CartPoleDiscreteBalancing, agent_rate 1000, physics_rate 1000 and real_time_factor float32 max
The environments are built on the Ignition Gazebo simulator through the ScenARIO project
The runtime is a gym.Env: class Runtime(gym.Env, abc.ABC)
The runtime step sets the task action, runs Gazebo and returns observation, reward, done and info
The runtime reset resets the task, runs a paused Gazebo step and returns the observation
The runtime seed method delegates to the task and returns the list of seeds
The task seeds its numpy RandomState with gym.utils.seeding.np_random(seed)
A cartpole reset draws x, dx, q and dq uniformly from -0.05 to 0.05
Action 1 commands +force_mag and any other action -force_mag as the linear joint's generalized force target
The cart limits are x 2.4 m, dx 20.0 m/s, q 12 degrees and dq 3*360 degrees per second
The observation is [x, dx, q, dq] taken from the linear and pivot joint positions and velocities
The observation space is the reset box scaled by 1.2
The episode is done when the observation leaves the reset box
The reward is 1.0 when not done and 0.0 when done, minus 0.10|x|, minus 0.10|dx| and minus 10.0 when x >= 0.9*2.4
One environment step runs physics_rate/agent_rate simulation iterations of 1.0/physics_rate seconds
Gym-ignition does not provide out-of-the-box environments; the environments package holds canonical examples

determinism.notes: the runtime seeds the task's numpy RandomState through gym.utils.seeding.np_random (base/task.py:234-239) and a reset draws from it; the fake backend implements the same protocol with Python's random.Random, so a seed repeats a trajectory within one implementation but not across the fake and the upstream environment

gaps: the fake backend is analytic: it moves the cart and pole positions directly and applies a fixed force; it models no rigid-body dynamics, contacts, friction, inertia or actuator, and the upstream Ignition Gazebo model was not run here
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor is 0 and the fake advances only when a step is requested (upstream registers real_time_factor as float32 max)
the fake draws the initial state with Python's random.Random while upstream draws it from numpy's RandomState, so one seed gives different trajectories on the two
observation values are Python floats in a list; upstream returns a numpy float32 array
the fake was never compared with an Ignition Gazebo run, and no physical device is modelled
snapshot and restore are not offered: the environment exposes no get_state/set_state

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
